subject: Vulnerability remediation attestation, forensic handoff & retention protocol
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finservco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@finservco.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: remediation attestation + retention proof for upcoming SOC2 audit

Kimberly —

As part of our SOC2 readiness window we need a formal attestation and supporting evidence for vulnerability management related to three recently reported CVEs that affected service components we integrate with. Specifically we need:

- A signed attestation that Redwood completed remediation for identified CVEs and the dates those fixes reached production.
- Evidence of scan cadence and the last three scan snapshots demonstrating closure (screencaps or exported reports).
- Retention policy and where forensic artifacts (scan logs, patch manifests, rollback traces) will be stored for a 3-year retention window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide these materials by Tuesday, 18 May? If you prefer, we can accept a compact packet (manifest + attest) and a link to the evidence bucket.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex Turner
Security Manager, FinServCo
alex.turner@finservco.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finservco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remediation attestation + retention proof for upcoming SOC2 audit

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can provide a compact evidence packet and the attestation you described. High level plan: 

1) Deliver a remediation manifest cataloging CVE IDs, owners, mitigation types (hotfix/backport/config), and production deployment timestamps — PDF + CSV.
2) Export the three most recent authenticated VM scan snapshots (the report export + CSV findings index).
3) Provide the retention policy excerpt and a signed statement confirming artifacts are retained in our secure evidence bucket (GCS, encrypted at rest) with 3-year retention and access audit logs.
4) Include patch-rollout logs (timestamps, nodes targeted, and verification checksums) and a short forensic handoff note for your auditors describing how to validate evidence provenance.

Marissa will compile the manifest and scan exports; Ben will provide the rollout logs and checksums. I will draft the attestation and sign it. We should be able to meet the Tuesday 18 May deadline.

To be safe: Marissa/Ben — could you confirm availability to assemble exports and attachment stubs by end of day Monday (17 May)?

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finservco.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: remediation attestation + retention proof for upcoming SOC2 audit

Kimberly / Alex —

Quick update: I pulled the last three authenticated scan exports and trimmed PII from the findings. Exports include:
- full-scan-export-20270401.csv (summary + findings)
- full-scan-export-20270415.csv
- full-scan-export-20270501.csv

I've also generated a condensed "manifest" view (redwood_vm_remediation_manifest_20270514.pdf) that maps each CVE to the remediation PR, rollout window, and verification checksum. That manifest references the patch-rollout-log (attached as CSV). All files are stamped with a hash and uploaded to the evidence folder (link below).

Notes on provenance: we digitally sign the manifest and record the upload event in our audit table; the audit record includes uploader, timestamp, and artifact hash. If auditors need a direct proof-of-hash email chain, we can export that too.

Link to evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Redwood-FinServ-evidence

Marissa Cole
Senior Security Operations Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finservco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Morgan Lee <audit@thirdparty-auditors.com>
Bcc: legal@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Final attestation and handoff: CVE remediation + retention protocol (FinServCo)

Alex / Morgan —

Please find attached the compact evidence packet and our formal attestation. Attachments: redwood_vm_remediation_manifest_20270514.pdf, patch-rollout-log-20270516.csv, cve-ownership-ledger-20270517.csv.

Attestation (signed):
Redwood Inference confirms that the CVEs listed in the attached remediation manifest were remediated and verified in production as described. Remediation deployment windows and verification checksums are included in the manifest. Evidence artifacts (scan exports, manifests, rollout logs) are retained in our encrypted evidence bucket for a minimum of three years from the date of upload. Access to retained artifacts is logged and audited; exports of access logs are available upon reasonable audit request.

If FinServCo requires a DocuSign-signed physical attestation, please reply and we will route the attestation through our legal signing flow.

Next steps / action items:
- Audit team (Morgan): let us know if you require additional artifact formats or expanded provenance exports (S3/GCS object version history, signed hash chain).
- Alex: confirm receipt and whether the attached packet satisfies the SOC2 evidence ask.

Thanks — and happy to hop on a short call if any of the auditors want a walkthrough.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_vm_remediation_manifest_20270514.pdf (signature block), patch-rollout-log-20270516.csv, cve-ownership-ledger-20270517.csv
